work: Hesiod, the Homeric Hymns, and Homerica

Zeus.what: Zeus punishes Prometheus's theft of fire by ordering the making of Pandora.
Zeus is hidden in Crete, then forces Cronos to disgorge his siblings.
Zeus hurls thunderbolts and defeats the Titans, who are chained in Tartarus.
Zeus strikes down Typhoeus and hurls him into Tartarus.
Zeus becomes king, swallows Metis and fathers Athene and many gods.
Zeus laughs at Hermes' denials and sends him and Apollo to recover the cattle.

Apollo.what: Apollo enters Zeus's hall and the gods tremble; Leto calms him.
Apollo is born on Delos, fed by Themis, and declares his gifts.
Apollo founds his oracle at Delphi and kills the dragoness.
Apollo leaps aboard the Cretan ship as a dolphin and names the crew his priests.
Apollo tracks the stolen cattle to Cyllene and confronts baby Hermes.
Apollo trades the herds for Hermes' lyre and gives him a golden staff.

Athena.what: Athene dresses the first woman fashioned by Hephaestus.
Athene is born armed from Zeus's head.
Athene advises Heracles and rides with him against Cycnus.
Athene warns Ares off and turns his spear as Heracles wounds him.
Athena springs armed from Zeus's head, shaking the cosmos until she removes her armour.
Athena plans vengeance on the Greeks after Aias offends her at Troy.

Cronos.what: Cronos castrates his father Heaven with Earth's sickle.
Cronos swallows his children and is tricked with a swaddled stone.
Cronos takes horse shape and fathers Cheiron on Philyra.

Heracles.what: Heracles is born to Alcmena and Zeus and confronts Cycnus and Ares.
Heracles arms with divine gifts and takes up his shield.
Heracles warns Cycnus and kills him with a spear thrust to the neck.
Heracles wounds Ares in the thigh and strips Cycnus's armour.
Heracles is hymned as mightiest mortal, now living on Olympus with Hebe.
Heracles besieges Themiscyra until Antiope betrays it.

Hermes.what: Hermes is born, invents the lyre, and steals Apollo's cattle on his first day.
Hermes roasts two cows, returns to his cradle, and defies Maia.
Hermes denies the theft to Apollo and demands judgement from Zeus.
Hermes brazenly denies theft before Zeus, then charms Apollo with his lyre.
Hermes gives Apollo the lyre in exchange for the herds and swears an oath.

Aphrodite.what: Aphrodite rises from the foam and goes to Cythera and Cyprus.
Aphrodite adorns herself at Paphos and meets Anchises on Ida.
Aphrodite lies with Anchises, reveals herself and foretells Aeneas.
Aphrodite tells Anchises the tale of Tithonus and warns him to keep silence.
Aphrodite is borne by the wind to Cyprus and adorned by the Hours.
Aphrodite wins the beauty contest and brings Alexandrus and Helen together.

Poseidon.what: Poseidon fathers Bellerophon and gives Periclymenus many shapes.
Poseidon is hymned as shaker of earth, horse-tamer and saviour of ships.

Hera.what: Hera blinds Teiresias for his answer about love.
Hera sets Argus to guard Io.
Hera keeps Eilithyia away from Leto out of envy.
Hera, angered at Zeus over Athena, bears Typhaon alone and gives him to the dragoness.
Hera is praised as queen of the immortals, wife and sister of Zeus.

Leto.what: Leto wanders seeking a home for Apollo and swears Delos's oath.
Leto gives birth to Apollo on Delos.

Demeter.what: Demeter searches for Persephone and wanders disguised to Eleusis.
Demeter, as Doso, tells a false tale and is made to smile by Iambe.
Demeter tries to make Demophoon immortal, reveals herself and orders a temple.
Demeter withholds the harvest and is reunited with Persephone.
Demeter makes earth fruitful again and teaches her mysteries.

Ares.what: Ares meets Heracles and Cycnus in Apollo's grove.
Ares attacks Heracles, is wounded in the thigh and flees to Olympus.
Ares is praised with many titles and prayed to for courage and peace.
Ares equips the Mice for war.

Artemis.what: Artemis turns Callisto into a bear.
Artemis drives her chariot to Claros where Apollo waits.
Artemis hunts, then leads the Muses and Graces in dance at Delphi.

Muses.what: The Muses dance on Helicon and give Hesiod the gift of song.
The poet names the Muses as sources of song and asks their favour.

Hephaestus.what: Hephaestus moulds Pandora from earth at Zeus's command.
Hephaestus fashions the first woman as Zeus's punishment.
Hephaestus made the decorated shield, with its many scenes.
Hephaestus is hymned as teacher of crafts with Athene.

Hades.what: Hades abducts Persephone with Zeus's consent.
Hades yields Persephone but secretly gives her a pomegranate seed.

Earth.what: Earth plots against Heaven and makes the sickle.
Earth hides Zeus in Crete and tricks Cronos with a stone.
Earth advises freeing the Hundred-Handers against the Titans.
Earth is hymned as eldest mother of all, nourishing every creature.

Helios.what: Helios tells Demeter that Zeus gave Persephone to Hades.
Helios drives his radiant chariot across the sky.

Hesiod.what: Hesiod warns the princes and urges Perses to justice and work.
Hesiod, tending lambs, receives a laurel rod and song from the Muses.
Hesiod poses riddling half-lines and questions to Homer.
Hesiod is crowned winner by King Paneides for praising peace and farming.
Hesiod is killed at Oenoe and his body is moved to Orchomenus.

Odysseus.what: Odysseus sends no gifts for Helen, knowing Menelaus will win.
Odysseus's feigned madness is exposed at the gathering of leaders.
Odysseus purifies Achilles and quarrels with Aias over his arms.
Odysseus wins Achilles' arms, spies in Ilium and takes the Palladium.
Odysseus murders Astyanax in the sack of Troy.
Odysseus marries Callidice and is killed by his son Telegonus.

Achilles.what: Peleus saves Achilles from Thetis's cauldron test.
Achilles raids the Troad and quarrels over prizes.
Achilles kills Penthesileia and Memnon, then is killed by Paris and Apollo.
Achilles' ghost foretells the fates of the fleet.

Homer.what: Homer trades riddles with fishermen about lice.
Homer's origin is disputed; he consults the Pythia and meets Hesiod.
Homer completes Hesiod's half-lines and wins praise for his feasting verses.
Homer answers all Hesiod's riddles but loses the crown to him.
Homer wanders reciting, writes Midas's epitaph, and dedicates a bowl at Delphi.
Homer recites the Hymn to Apollo at Delos and dies at Ios.

Maia.what: Maia bears Hermes to Zeus in secret in a cave on Cyllene.
Maia scolds Hermes for roaming at night.
Shy Maia secretly lies with Zeus while Hera sleeps.

Ocean.what: Ocean fathers the rivers and the Oceanids with Tethys.

Helen.what: Helen is wooed by many suitors; Aphrodite shames Tyndareus's daughters.
Helen is courted at Tyndareus' house; Menelaus wins her.
Alexandrus takes Helen from Sparta to Troy.
Helen is born to Nemesis and Zeus and abducted.
Menelaus finds Helen at the sack and takes her to the ships.

Themis.what: Themis marries Zeus and bears the Hours and Fates.
Themis feeds the newborn Apollo nectar and ambrosia.
Themis helps Zeus plan the Trojan war.

Thetis.what: Thetis refuses Zeus and is doomed to marry a mortal.
Thetis tests her children by Peleus in a cauldron.
Thetis refuses Zeus to please Hera and weds Peleus.
Thetis mourns Achilles and carries him to the White Island.

Agamemnon.what: Agamemnon woos Helen on Menelaus' behalf.
Agamemnon offends Artemis and Iphigeneia is nearly sacrificed.
Agamemnon is murdered by Aegisthus and Clytaemnestra.

Menelaus.what: Menelaus wins Helen with the greatest gifts.
Menelaus learns of Helen's abduction and plans war.
Menelaus finds Helen at Troy's fall and takes her to the ships.
Menelaus reaches Egypt with five ships.

Rhea.what: Rhea bears children to Cronos and plots with Earth to save Zeus.
Rhea brings Zeus's settlement to Demeter.

Alcmena.what: Alcmena survives her brothers' deaths and bears Heracles to Zeus.
Alcmena lies with Zeus and bears twins Heracles and Iphiclus.

Dionysus.what: Dionysus is born in secret to Zeus and Semele, honoured by Zeus's nod.
Dionysus is seized by pirates and turns the ship to wonders.
Dionysus is raised by Nymphs at Nysa and roams the woods.

Iris.what: Iris fetches Styx's water for the gods' oath.
Iris is sent by Zeus to summon Demeter.
Iris persuades Eilithyia away from Hera to Leto.

Peleus.what: Peleus is plotted against by Acastus and marries Thetis.
Peleus stops Thetis before she tests Achilles.
Peleus weds Thetis on Pelion and receives gifts.

Perses.what: Hesiod addresses Perses and warns him against litigation.
Perses is urged to choose justice and work.
Perses is rebuked for begging and given advice on wealth and farming.
Perses is told to beach his ship in winter and sail only in season.

Atlas.what: Atlas holds up the sky as punishment.
Atlas holds up heaven by the house of Night.

Cheiron.what: Cheiron is born a centaur to Cronos and Philyra.
Cheiron gives Peleus an ashen spear.

Circe.what: Circe comes to her western island on the Sun's chariot.
Circe makes Odysseus' family immortal after Telegonus kills him.

Eos.what: Eos wins deathlessness for Tithonus but forgets youth.
Eos wins immortality for her son Memnon.

Diomedes.what: Diomedes fetches Philoctetes and helps take the Palladium.

Heaven.what: Heaven hides his children and is castrated by Cronos.
Heaven advises Zeus to swallow Metis.

Iolaus.what: Iolaus drives Heracles' chariot to meet Cycnus and Ares.
Iolaus encourages Heracles to arm for the fight.
Iolaus drives the chariot as Heracles kills Cycnus.
Iolaus helps strip Cycnus's armour and goes to Trachis.

Selene.what: Selene drives her horses across the sky and bears Pandia to Zeus.

Night.what: Night is born of Chaos and bears Aether and Day.
Night bears Doom, Death, Sleep, the Fates and many afflictions.
Night's house stands in Tartarus, home of Sleep and Death.

Oedipus.what: Oedipus dies at Thebes and is mourned.
Oedipus curses his sons Polyneices and Eteocles.

Persephone.what: Persephone is seized by Aidoneus while picking flowers.
Persephone eats the pomegranate seed and tells her tale.
Persephone is reunited with Demeter and will spend a third of the year below.

Aeetes.what: Aeetes' daughter Medea is taken by Iason.
Phrixus enters the halls of Aeetes with the fleece.

Aeneas.what: Aphrodite foretells Aeneas as son of Anchises who will rule the Trojans.

Briareos.what: Briareos is freed by Zeus on Earth's advice.
Briareos and the Hundred-Handers bury and chain the Titans.

Semele.what: Semele is greeted as mother of Dionysus.

Castor.what: Castor and the twins appear on tawny wings to calm storms.
Castor is killed by Idas in a cattle raid.
Castor, mortal, is spied by Lynceus and killed by Idas.

Strife.what: Hesiod distinguishes two Strifes, one harmful and one wholesome.
Strife disrupts the wedding feast of Peleus.

Hecate.what: Hecate is honoured above all by Zeus and aids many.
Hecate hears Persephone's cry and helps Demeter search.

Iphiclus.what: Iphiclus the swift runner skims over ears of corn.
Iphiclus is born as Heracles' weaker twin.

Nestor.what: Nestor alone escapes Heracles' slaughter of Neleus's sons.

Polydeuces.what: Polydeuces and Castor calm storms for sailors.
Polydeuces kills Lynceus and Idas and shares immortality.
Polydeuces, immortal, is spied by Lynceus with Castor.

Telemachus.what: Telemachus is taken to Circe and made immortal.

Theseus.what: Theseus carries Helen off before the Dioscuri sack Aphidna and Athens.
Antiope, in love with Theseus, betrays Themiscyra to Heracles.

Aias.what: Aias of Salamis comes among the suitors to woo Helen.
Aias and Odysseus save Achilles' body; they then quarrel over his arms.
Aias goes mad after losing Achilles' arms and dies.
Aias offends Athena by dragging Cassandra from her image at the sack of Troy.

Amphitryon.what: Amphitryon, exiled for killing Alcmena's father, goes to war while Zeus lies with Alcmena.

Anchises.what: Anchises, alone on Ida, meets Aphrodite disguised as a maiden and prays to her.
Anchises takes Aphrodite to bed, then is terrified when she reveals herself.
Aphrodite tells Anchises of Tithonus and instructs him about their son.

Boreas.what: Boreas sweeps from Thrace in the month Lenaeon, freezing beasts and old men.
Boreas is named among the beneficial winds, unlike Typhoeus' harmful ones.

Celeus.what: Celeus hears the story, assembles the people and has Demeter's temple built.
Celeus is among the kings Demeter teaches her mysteries.

Graces.what: The Graces bathe and dress Aphrodite at Paphos.
The Graces join Artemis in dance at Delphi.

Cottus.what: Cottus pledges the freed Hundred-Handers' aid to Zeus against the Titans.
Cottus and his brothers bury and chain the Titans in Tartarus.

Cycnus.what: Cycnus ignores Heracles' warning, fights him and is killed by a spear thrust.
Ceyx buries Cycnus, but the river Anaurus erases the grave.

Gyes.what: Gyes is freed from beneath the earth to fight the Titans.
Gyes and his brothers bury and chain the Titans in Tartarus.

Hestia.what: Hestia is named among the three goddesses Aphrodite cannot move, vowed to virginity.
Hestia is honoured first and last at every feast and invoked with Hermes.

Lycaon.what: Lycaon serves Zeus a butchered babe; his daughter Callisto becomes a constellation.

Medea.what: Medea is brought by Iason from Aeetes to Iolcus and bears Medeus.
Medea makes Aeson young again with a brew of herbs.
Medea poisons Creon, flees to Athens, and her sons are killed at Hera's altar.

Mnemosyne.what: Mnemosyne lies nine nights with Zeus and bears the nine Muses.

Minos.what: Minos is born to Zeus and Europa in Crete.

Nymphs.what: The mountain Nymphs will rear Aphrodite's son by Anchises.
The Nymphs raise Dionysus at Nysa and follow him through the woods.

Oeneus.what: Oeneus receives Periboea sent by her father Hipponous.
Oeneus marries Periboea, or gets her as a prize after Olenus falls.

Prometheus.what: Prometheus steals fire in a fennel-stalk, angering Zeus.
Prometheus tricks Zeus at Mecone with bones hidden under fat, and is bound.
Zeus punishes Prometheus' theft by having the first woman fashioned.

Tyndareus.what: Aphrodite, angered at Tyndareus, makes his daughters desert their husbands.
Tyndareus binds Helen's suitors by oath and awards her to Menelaus.

Typhaon.what: Typhaon and Echidna produce Cerberus, the Hydra, Chimaera, the Sphinx and others.
Hera bears Typhaon in anger at Zeus and gives him to the dragoness.

Aeacus.what: Aeacus, lonely, receives a people when Zeus turns ants into men.

Alexandrus.what: Alexandrus judges the goddesses, chooses Aphrodite, and takes Helen to Troy.

Amphiaraus.what: Foreseeing his fate, Amphiaraus is swallowed by the earth with his chariot.

Andromache.what: Andromache is given to Neoptolemus after Troy's fall.

Antiope.what: Antiope grows up in Hyria; her sons build Thebes' walls.
Antiope betrays Themiscyra to Heracles for love of Theseus.

Argus.what: Argus watches Io as a white cow and is killed by Hermes.

Asclepius.what: Zeus kills Asclepius with a thunderbolt.
Asclepius is born to Coronis in the Dotian plain and hailed as healer.

Bread-nibbler.what: Bread-nibbler hosts the Mice's assembly and rises to speak.

Calchas.what: Calchas loses the fig riddle contest to Mopsus and dies of vexation.

Callidice.what: Callidice proposes that Metaneira take the stranger in as nurse.
Odysseus marries Callidice, Queen of the Thesprotians.

Calliope.what: Calliope is invoked to sing of Helios.

Ceyx.what: Ceyx buries Cycnus after Heracles kills him.
Heracles often visits Ceyx at Trachis.

Chryseis.what: Chryseis is given to Agamemnon as a prize.

Coeus.what: Coeus and Phoebe have Leto, Asteria and Hecate.

Coronis.what: Coronis weds Ischys; Zeus kills her son Asclepius.
Coronis bears Asclepius in the Dotian plain.

Creon.what: Medea poisons Creon, the ruler of Corinth.

Crumb-snatcher.what: Crumb-snatcher rides Puff-jaw's back across the lake and drowns when the frog dives.

Dardanus.what: Dardanus is born to Electra and Zeus and founds the Trojan line.

Eilithyia.what: Hera keeps Eilithyia on Olympus while Leto labours.
Iris persuades Eilithyia with a necklace; Leto bears Apollo.

Electra.what: Electra bears Dardanus and Eetion to Zeus.

Hours.what: The Hours dress Aphrodite in gold and present her to the gods.

Nemesis.what: Nemesis flees Zeus through many shapes, is caught and bears Helen.

Iphigeneia.what: Iphigeneia is nearly sacrificed after Agamemnon offends Artemis, but is rescued.

Lynceus.what: Lynceus climbs Taygetus and sees Castor and Polydeuces hidden in an oak.

Memnon.what: Memnon comes to help Troy, kills Antilochus, and is killed by Achilles.

Neoptolemus.what: Neoptolemus is fetched from Scyros, kills Eurypylus, and later Priam and Astyanax.
Neoptolemus kills Priam and takes Andromache.

Philoctetes.what: Philoctetes is brought from Lemnos, healed, and kills Alexandrus.

Phineus.what: Phineus is blinded, and the Harpies carry him off.
Phineus is blinded for guiding Phrixus.

Phrixus.what: Phrixus is carried off by the golden ram.
Phrixus brings the fleece to Aeetes, purifies it after sacrifice and enters his halls.

Protesilaus.what: Protesilaus dies at Troy, killed by Hector on landing.
Protesilaus is the first Greek to land at Troy.

Puff-jaw.what: Puff-jaw meets Crumb-snatcher, ferries him across the lake, then dives and drowns him.
Puff-jaw denies guilt for the mouse's death and proposes a plan; the Frogs arm.

Styx.what: Styx joins Zeus first against the Titans and becomes the gods' oath.
Styx lives apart; Iris fetches her water for the gods' oath.

Teiresias.what: Teiresias changes sex, judges love for Zeus and Hera, and is blinded by Hera.
Teiresias lives seven generations and complains to Zeus that long life is no honour.

Telegonus.what: Telegonus lands on Ithaca, kills Odysseus unwittingly, and takes the family to Circe.

Telephus.what: Telephus is born to Auge and Heracles and later routs the Achaeans.
Telephus fights the Greeks who mistakenly sack Teuthrania.

Adrastus.what: Adrastus flees Thebes on Areion and laments Amphiaraus among the seven dead.

Aeson.what: Aeson is made young again by Medea with a brew of herbs.

Aethra.what: Aethra is rescued from Troy by Theseus' sons.

Amphion.what: Amphion and Zethus build the walls of Thebes with a lyre.

Arion.what: Adrastus escapes Thebes on the horse Areion.

Argea.what: Argeia and others come to mourn Oedipus after he dies.

Ariadne.what: Ariadne is deserted by Theseus for Aegle.

Astyanax.what: Astyanax is thrown from a tower at the sack of Troy.
Astyanax is killed in the sack of Troy.

Bellerophon.what: Bellerophon, son of Poseidon, rides Pegasus and kills the Chimera.

Callisto.what: Callisto is seduced by Zeus, turned into a bear, and made a constellation.

Cassandra.what: Cassandra is dragged away by Aias in the sack of Troy.

Cephalus.what: Cephalus, purified by the Cadmeans, hunts the Teumesian fox with his hound; both turn to stone.

Passalus.what: Passalus and his brother Acmon roam deceiving people, warned by their mother about Heracles.

Ceto.what: Ceto bears the Graiae and Gorgons.
Ceto and Phorcys have their youngest child, the snake guarding the golden apples.

Chimaera.what: The Chimera is slain by Bellerophon.

Chrysaor.what: Chrysaor is born from Medusa when Perseus beheads her.

Clymene.what: Clymene marries Phylacus and bears the swift runner Iphiclus.

Clytaemnestra.what: Clytaemnestra deserts Agamemnon for Aegisthus, shamed by Aphrodite.

Cretans.what: The Cretan sailors are seized by Apollo as a dolphin and steered to Crisa.
The Cretans build an altar, follow Apollo to Parnassus and become his temple servants.

Cretheus.what: Tyro's sons by Poseidon and Cretheus are traced, with Cretheus as her husband.

Idaean Dactyls.what: The Idaean Dactyls teach iron smelting and tempering in Crete.

Danae.what: Perseus, son of Danae, flees the Gorgons on the shield.

Day.what: Day passes Night at the bronze threshold.

Deiphobus.what: Deiphobus is killed by Menelaus in the sack of Troy.

Electryon.what: Electryon's sons are killed by the Taphians, leaving Alcmena alone.

Endymion.what: Endymion receives from Zeus the choice of when to die.
Endymion is taken to heaven, then cast down to Hades for desiring Hera.

Epimetheus.what: Epimetheus accepts Pandora, who opens the jar and looses evils.
Epimetheus is named as the scatter-brained son of Iapetus.

Erinyes.what: The Erinyes spring from the blood of the castrated Heaven.

Eumolpus.what: Eumolpus is taught Demeter's mysteries with the other Eleusinian kings.

Europa.what: Zeus carries Europa to Crete as a bull and fathers three sons.

Euryale.what: Euryale, daughter of Minos, is named as the mother of Orion.

Eurynome.what: Glaucus woos the wise Eurynome, who bears Bellerophon to Poseidon.

Eurypylus.what: Eurypylus, Trojan ally, is killed by Neoptolemus.

Ganymede.what: Ganymede is carried off by an eagle.
Ganymedes is taken by Zeus to be cupbearer and made immortal.

Geryones.what: Geryones, three-headed owner of oxen, is killed by Heracles.

Glaucus.what: Glaucus woos Eurynome, but Zeus decrees his children will not be his own.

Gorgons.what: The Gorgons chase Perseus as he flees with the Gorgon's head.

Helenus.what: Helenus is captured by Odysseus and prophesies.

Hermione.what: Hermione is born to Helen and Menelaus.

Hipponous.what: Hipponous sends his seduced daughter Periboea to Oeneus with orders to kill her.

Iason.what: Iason completes Pelias' labours and brings Medea home to Iolcus.
Iason is born to Aeson and raised by Chiron.

Idas.what: Idas and Lynceus fight Castor and Polydeuces.
Idas kills Castor after Lynceus spies the Dioscuri in the oak.

Iphianassa.what: The daughters of Proetus go mad and are cured by Melampus.

Leda.what: Leda bears the twins Castor and Polydeuces to Zeus beneath Taygetus.
Leda bears Castor and Polydeuces to Zeus beneath Mount Taygetus.

Lick-platter.what: Lick-platter sees the drowning and tells the Mice.

Manto.what: Manto is sent to Delphi, marries Rhacius, and weeps at Colophon.

Melampus.what: Melampus cures the mad daughters of Proetus.
Melampus gains prophecy from a serpent's young and escapes Iphiclus.

Meleager.what: Meleager slays the Calydonian boar and dies fighting the Curetes.

Metaneira.what: Metaneira welcomes Demeter and asks her to nurse her late-born son.
Metaneira spies Demeter putting Demophoon in the fire and cries out, ruining the gift.

Midas.what: A bronze maiden speaks, marking the tomb of Midas.
Homer writes the epitaph for Midas's tomb.

Mopsus.what: Mopsus beats Calchas in the fig riddle contest, and Calchas dies of vexation.

Nike.what: Nike is born to Styx and joins Zeus against the Titans.

Old man.what: The old vine-tender at Onchestus sees Hermes and is bribed to stay silent.
The old man tells Apollo of a child driving cattle backwards.

Orion.what: Orion is blinded, healed, killed by a scorpion, and set among the stars.

Pandora.what: Pandora is made by the gods, accepted by Epimetheus, and opens the jar of evils.

Paneides.what: King Paneides judges the contest and crowns Hesiod for praising peace and farming.

Pegasus.what: Pegasus is born from Medusa when Perseus beheads her.
Pegasus is ridden by Bellerophon, who kills the Chimera.

Penelope.what: Penelope is taken by Telegonus to Circe, who makes her immortal.

Periboea.what: Periboea is seduced and sent by her father to Oeneus.
Oeneus marries Periboea or receives her as a prize.

Periclymenus.what: Periclymenus shape-shifts, attacks Heracles, and is shot through Athene's scheme.
Periclymenus is named in the Thebaid as killer of Parthenopaeus.

Perseus.what: Golden Perseus flies with winged sandals, fleeing the Gorgons.

Phorcys.what: Phorcys fathers the Graiae and Gorgons with Ceto.

Phylacus.what: Phylacus marries Clymene, who bears the swift Iphiclus.

Polynices.what: Polyneices sets Cadmus' table and cup before Oedipus, who curses him.

Polyxeinus.what: Polyxeinus is taught Demeter's mysteries among the Eleusinian princes.

Pot-visitor.what: Pot-visitor, the Mouse herald, carries the challenge to the Frogs.
Blameless Pot-visitor kills Brewer in the slaughter along the shore.

Priam.what: Priam is killed by Neoptolemus in the night sack.
Priam is killed at the altar in the sack of Troy.

Rhadamanthys.what: Rhadamanthys is born to Zeus and Europa in Crete.

Sarpedon.what: Sarpedon rules Lycia and fights at Troy as a Trojan ally.

Sinon.what: Sinon shows the signal-light in the night sack of Ilium.
Sinon signals the Greek fleet, who storm Troy.

Sphinx.what: The Sphinx is born to Echidna and Typhaon, destroyer of the Cadmeans.
The Sphinx kills Haemon, son of Creon, in the Story of Oedipus.

Tartarus.what: Tartarus arises among the first powers, a dim place deep in the Earth.
Tartarus is father of Typhoeus and receives him when Zeus hurls him down.

Telphusa.what: Telphusa tricks Apollo into building his oracle at Crisa instead of her spring.
Apollo buries Telphusa's spring under rocks for her deception.

Tethys.what: Tethys bears to Ocean the rivers and the three thousand Oceanids.

Tithonus.what: Tithonus, given deathlessness without youth by Eos, withers into babbling old age.

Triptolemus.what: Triptolemus is taught Demeter's mysteries among the Eleusinian princes.

Acastus.what: Acastus plots against Peleus, hiding his knife so the Centaurs will kill him.

Aidos.what: Aidos departs from mankind with Nemesis as the iron age declines.

Amphilochus.what: Amphilochus is killed by Apollo at Soli.

Anaurus.what: The river Anaurus washes away Cycnus's grave at Apollo's command.

Antilochus.what: Antilochus is slain by Memnon and buried by the Achaeans.

Arcas.what: Son of Callisto and Zeus, Arcas nearly kills his bear-mother and becomes the constellation Bootes.

Argives.what: The Argives, delighted by Homer's praise, give him gifts, a bronze statue and sacrifices.

Asphodicus.what: Asphodicus is said by the Thebans to have killed Parthenopaeus.

Atalanta.what: Atalanta refuses marriage and races Hippomenes, who beats her with Aphrodite's golden apples.

Auge.what: Auge, taken in by Teuthras, bears Telephus to Heracles.

Battus.what: Battus betrays Hermes' cattle theft for a robe and is turned to rock.

Cabbage-climber.what: Cabbage-climber throws mud and has his shin splintered in the fighting.

Cedalion.what: Cedalion, servant of Hephaestus, guides the blinded Orion.

Crabs.what: Sent by Zeus, the Crabs nip off the Mice's tails and paws and rout them.

Croakperson.what: Croakperson disembowels Crumb-snatcher in the battle.

Ctimenus.what: Ctimenus, in Eratosthenes' version, kills Hesiod with his brother over their sister.

Delians.what: The Delians dedicate Homer's Hymn to Apollo in the temple of Artemis.

Delos.what: Delos fears Apollo's pride and bargains with Leto, demanding an oath before agreeing.

Demophoon.what: Demophoon is nursed by Demeter, anointed with ambrosia and hidden in the fire; his immortality is lost.

Dread.what: Dread, with Panic, carries the wounded Ares to Olympus.

Dryops' daughter.what: Dryops' daughter weds Hermes and bears Pan, whose appearance terrifies the nurse.

Echidna.what: Echidna lives in a cave in Arima and bears monsters with Typhaon.

Eriphyle.what: Eriphyle bears Alcmaon to Amphiaraus, whose chariot the earth swallows.

Eteocles.what: Eteocles and Polyneices are cursed by Oedipus to strife.

Eurycles.what: Eurycles the seer sacrifices to atone for the killers of Hesiod.

Eurylochus.what: Eurylochus drives the snake out, and Demeter receives it at Eleusis

Eurytion.what: Eurytion, herdsman of Geryones, is killed by Heracles

Fisherman.what: Fishermen answer Homer with a riddle about lice

Ganyctor.what: Ganyctor holds funeral games for his father Amphidamas, where the contest takes place

Gnawer.what: Gnawer sends his son Slice-snatcher to war against the Frogs

Hadrian.what: Hadrian consults the Pythia, who tells him Homer's origin

Haemon.what: Haemon, son of Creon, is killed by the Sphinx

Ham-nibbler.what: Ham-nibbler is killed by a pebble in the battle

Harpies.what: The Harpies are chased across the world by the Sons of Boreas

hawk.what: The hawk carries off the nightingale and mocks her, asserting the right of the strong

helmsman.what: The helmsman recognises Dionysus as a god, urges freeing him, and is spared

Hippomenes.what: Hippomenes tricks Atalanta with golden apples and wins the race

Hope.what: Hope stays inside the jar when Pandora looses evils

Hymenaeus.what: Hymenaeus is loved by Apollo; Hermes steals his cattle

Iambe.what: Iambe makes grieving Demeter smile with her jests

Io.what: Io is seduced by Zeus, turned into a white cow and guarded by Argus

Ionians.what: The Ionians gather at Delos and make Homer a citizen of every state.

Iphinoe.what: Iphinoe, with her sisters, goes mad for scorning a god and is cured by Melampus.

Ischys.what: Ischys weds Coronis, as a crow tells Phoebus.

Justice.what: Justice, daughter of Zeus, is dragged by bribe-eating judges and reports wrongs to her father.

Laocoon.what: Laocoon is killed with a son by serpents as the Trojans debate the horse.

Locrian Aias.what: Locrian Aias dies in the storm at Capherides on the voyage home.

Lysippe.what: Lysippe, with her sisters, goes mad for scorning a god and is cured by Melampus.

Margites.what: Margites, a foolish man who knows many things badly, fails at every craft.

master.what: The master scorns the helmsman's warning and orders the ship to sail on with Dionysus.
The master is killed by the lion as Dionysus transforms himself aboard.

Medon.what: King Medon of Athens hosts Homer, who improvises verses by the fire.

Medusa.what: Medusa bears Chrysaor and Pegasus when Perseus beheads her.

Meliae.what: The Meliae spring from the blood of Heaven's castration.

Menoetius.what: Menoetius is struck down by Zeus's thunderbolt.

Merope.what: Merope is outraged by Orion, who is then blinded by her father Oenopion.

Metis.what: Metis is wed by Zeus, then swallowed to prevent a rival king.

Mother of the Gods.what: The Mother of the Gods is hymned as delighting in rattles, timbrels, flutes and wild beasts' cries.

Muck-coucher.what: Muck-coucher, a faultless Mouse, kills Lick-platter in the shore fighting.

nightingale.what: The nightingale, seized in the hawk's talons, is mocked by him as foolish to resist.

Oenomaus.what: Oenomaus kills the suitors of Hippodamia in the chariot race.

Oenopion.what: Oenopion, King of Chios, blinds Orion after Orion outrages Merope.

Orestes.what: Orestes avenges the murder of Agamemnon.

Pan.what: Pan is born to Hermes in Arcadia, terrifying his nurse; the gods delight in him and name him.

Pandia.what: Pandia is born to Selene and the Son of Cronos.

Panic.what: Panic and Dread carry the wounded Ares in his chariot to Olympus.

Paris.what: Paris, aided by Apollo, kills Achilles.

Parthenopaeus.what: Parthenopaeus is killed in battle, by Periclymenus according to the Thebaid.

Pelias.what: Pelias sets labours for Iason, who completes them and brings Medea home.

Penthesileia.what: Penthesileia fights for Troy and is killed by Achilles.

Persuasion.what: Persuasion helps the gods adorn Pandora.

Philyra.what: Philyra lies with Cronos, who takes horse shape, and bears the centaur Cheiron.

Polyxena.what: Polyxena is sacrificed at Achilles' tomb after Troy falls.

Pond-larker.what: Pond-larker fights among the Frogs in the first battle.

Proclus.what: Proclus notes that some editors attach the Divination by Birds to Works and Days.

Proetus.what: Proetus' daughters go mad for scorning a god and are cured by Melampus.

Rhacius.what: Rhacius is sent by oracle to marry Manto, who weeps at Colophon.

Rueful.what: Rueful alone among the Frogs shows prowess, then dives away.

Schoeneus.what: Schoeneus announces that Hippomenes may win Atalanta only by surviving a race.

Sleep.what: Sleep dwells with Night and Death, kind to men.

Slice-snatcher.what: Slice-snatcher dons chestnut-husk armour and routs the Frogs into the lake.

Sons of Boreas.what: The Sons of Boreas chase the Harpies past the strange peoples of the world's edge.

Tantalus.what: Tantalus asks the gods for endless pleasures and has a stone hung over him.

Teumesian fox.what: The Teumesian fox is hunted by Cephalus' hound, and both turn to stone.

Teuthras.what: Teuthras takes in Auge, who bears Telephus to Heracles.

Thersites.what: Thersites is killed by Achilles for reviling him.

Timandra.what: Timandra, with her sisters, is made by angry Aphrodite to desert her husband Echemus.

Titans.what: The Titans fight the gods, are buried under rocks by the Hundred-Handers and chained in Tartarus.

Trojans.what: The Trojans debate the wooden horse, dedicate it to Athena and feast, unaware of the Greeks inside.

Trophonius.what: Trophonius and Agamedes lay the stone footing of Apollo's temple at Delphi.

Tyro.what: Tyro bears sons to Poseidon and Cretheus, ancestors of the line leading to Iason.

Tyrsenian pirates.what: The Tyrsenian pirates seize Dionysus, ignore the helmsman's warning, and sail on.
Terrified by the wonders aboard, the pirates leap overboard and become dolphins.

Zethus.what: Zethus and Amphion build the walls of Thebes, Amphion using a lyre.

Iapetus.what: Iapetus's sons receive their fates: Menoetius struck down, Atlas bears the sky, Prometheus is bound.

Theia.what: Theia bears the Sun, Moon and Dawn to Hyperion.

Amphidamas.what: Hesiod wins a tripod at the funeral games of Amphidamas at Chalcis.

Creophylus.what: Homer sails toward his friend Creophylus at Ios, where he dies.

Agamedes.what: Agamedes and Trophonius lay the stone footing of Apollo's temple at Delphi.

Apollonius of Rhodes.what: Apollonius of Rhodes rejects the Divination by Birds as spurious.

Aristophanes.what: Aristophanes rejects the Precepts of Chiron as Hesiod's work.

Callithoe.what: Callithoe and her sisters see Demeter at the Maiden Well in Eleusis

Celmis.what: Celmis is credited with discovering iron in Cyprus with Damnameneus

Chaos.what: Chaos is the first thing to come to be, before Earth

Cinaethon.what: Cinaethon is named as the poet credited with the Story of Oedipus

Cleisidice.what: Cleisidice and her sisters see Demeter at the Maiden Well in Eleusis

Cychreus.what: Cychreus' snake is received by Demeter at Eleusis

Damnameneus.what: Damnameneus is credited with discovering iron in Cyprus with Celmis

Death.what: Death, pitiless son of Night, dwells in her house with Sleep

Deianeira.what: Deianeira unknowingly does a fearful thing with the poisoned robe

Delas.what: Delas, called Scythes, is credited with discovering bronze smelting

Demo.what: Demo and her sisters see Demeter at the Maiden Well in Eleusis

Epeius.what: Epeius builds the wooden horse that the Trojans bring into their city.

Lebes.what: Rhacius's father Lebes is named as the man Manto marries Rhacius son of.

Leeky.what: Leeky drags Lick-platter and later hurls a reed in the battle.

Medeus.what: Medeus is born to Medea at Iolcus after Iason brings her home.

Phegeus.what: Phegeus is named as father of the brothers who kill Hesiod at Oenoe

Stheneboea.what: Stheneboea, wife of Proetus, is named among the household of Proetus's daughters' madness story.

Telemon.what: Telemon kills Melanippe, according to a quoted fragment.

Tros.what: Tros is consoled by Zeus with horses for the loss of his son Ganymedes.

Water-larked.what: Water-larked, a Frog, kills the Mouse Ham-nibbler in the battle.
